title: I built something like Suno/Bolt, but for games - would anyone actually use this?
author: DisciplineWhich9244
selftext:
I’ve been working on a platform where you can basically describe a game in a prompt and the AI builds it for you.

The idea is pretty simple:

* You enter a prompt like *“Create a multiplayer survival game on a small island”*
* The platform generates the game
* You can continue editing it with more prompts
* You can save everything into separate projects
* You can come back later and keep working on your games
* And eventually you can publish/play the games with other people, including multiplayer

So it’s kind of **Suno/Bolt, but focused on playable games** rather than music or websites.

I already have a working version and I’m wondering whether it’s worth actually putting it online and developing it further.

**Would you personally use something like this?**  
And if it existed, what would you expect it to be able to do before you’d actually pay/use it?

I’m especially interested in whether the concept itself sounds useful or if there are already too many similar AI game generators.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: For me, how I would edit my games is this: I would prompt it in Claude code in it until I no longer able to get it to look right. Then I told him to create an editor for me so that I can manually fine tune that particular asset.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
You're just describing Claude Code. It can do everything except the publish part.

>Would you personally use something like this?

I would not, because it doesn't offer me anything worth switching away from Claude Code for. CC is way more flexible than this platform will be and will often do things, on its own, that are extremely helpful to development that your platform isn't capable of.

For example, in the game I'm working on, Claude has made about 3 different utility pages that show me every model in the game, let me fine-tune gun positions on my own and save them as project defaults, and I even had it make me a map editor so I can fix small issues myself like pickups being stuck in geometry or floating boxes.

comments.author: BlahajWithBenefits
comments.body:
People here probably won’t. A tool like that is for people that aren’t already doing ai game dev, its like the stepping stone for it.

But if you make it user friendly enough it would probably go crazy. Especially if people can publish and play the games others made. Kids/teens would be the initial audience, they already do it in fortnite and roblox and stuff. 

It needs to be as seamless and easy as those things are though.
